before.Presentation: Jamie Taylor, a 37-year-old woman, visits the clinic with right-upper-quadrant pain that persists between meals, nausea and a neutrophil count above the laboratory reference range. The common duct is not dilated; bilirubin is within the laboratory reference range.

MR cholangiopancreatography assessing the extrahepatic ducts

before: **KEY:** Hepatobiliary scintigraphy assessing gallbladder filling
Persistent local inflammatory findings call for assessment of gallbladder filling/cystic-duct obstruction despite the ultrasound components.
Hepatobiliary scintigraphy measuring stimulated ejection fraction
Confuses evaluation of chronic gallbladder emptying with evaluation of the acute inflammatory presentation.
MR cholangiopancreatography assessing the extrahepatic ducts
Prioritizes a duct-stone question over the gallbladder question suggested by persistent local signs; it is not a claim that MRI is never appropriate after ultrasound.
after: **KEY:** Hepatobiliary scintigraphy assessing gallbladder filling
Persistent local inflammatory findings call for assessment of gallbladder filling/cystic-duct obstruction despite the ultrasound components.
Hepatobiliary scintigraphy measuring stimulated ejection fraction
Confuses evaluation of chronic gallbladder emptying with evaluation of the acute inflammatory presentation.
MR cholangiopancreatography assessing the extrahepatic ducts
Prioritizes a duct-stone question over the gallbladder question suggested by persistent local signs; it is not a claim that MRI is never appropriate after ultrasound.

inference: Integrate persistent focal inflammatory findings with ultrasound components rather than treating a normal wall as exclusion. Then Distinguish gallbladder filling, stimulated emptying and extrahepatic-duct protocols.
focus: Melissa must confirm the exact protocol ranking. This does not claim a universal HIDA-over-all-CT/MRI algorithm; the former broad competing modalities have been replaced.

originalAuthoringBefore.Task: Which interpretation best accounts for Jamie Taylor's nipple-discharge history?
Options: **KEY:** Pathologic left-sided episodes; physiologic expressed secretion
Physiologic left-sided episodes; physiologic expressed secretion
Endocrine-mediated left-sided episodes; endocrine-mediated expressed secretion

comparisonBasis: Exact independently passed version retained from review six; both sides show the same clinical fields.

before: **KEY:** Continue breast evaluation; review metoclopramide and reassess prolactin
Separates the focal spontaneous discharge from the expressed bilateral component and addresses a plausible medication effect in parallel.
Continue breast evaluation; obtain pituitary MRI before medication review
Addresses the breast but treats a potentially medication-related prolactin rise as an established reason to prioritize pituitary imaging.
Defer breast evaluation; review metoclopramide and reassess prolactin
Makes evaluation of the spontaneous focal discharge contingent on resolution of a separate systemic finding.
Defer breast evaluation; obtain pituitary MRI before medication review
Combines drug-first delay of the focal workup with premature central imaging before assessment of the medication contribution.
after: **KEY:** Continue breast evaluation; review metoclopramide and reassess prolactin
Separates the focal spontaneous discharge from the expressed bilateral component and addresses a plausible medication effect in parallel.
Continue breast evaluation; obtain pituitary MRI before medication review
Addresses the breast but treats a potentially medication-related prolactin rise as an established reason to prioritize pituitary imaging.
Defer breast evaluation; review metoclopramide and reassess prolactin
Makes evaluation of the spontaneous focal discharge contingent on resolution of a separate systemic finding.
Defer breast evaluation; obtain pituitary MRI before medication review
Combines drug-first delay of the focal workup with premature central imaging before assessment of the medication contribution.

inference: Separate the spontaneous left-duct episodes from the bilateral expressed secretion and the medication-associated laboratory finding. Then Select parallel breast and medication evaluation rather than delaying the local workup or prematurely escalating the endocrine workup.
focus: Moderate application prediction only. The guideline-supported medication step is coordinated review, not an unsupervised drug stop or a diagnosis of a prolactinoma.
